title: Backtesting VaR: Exceedance vs PIT

maps.tested: Reported by name in two separate sittings' recalls and marked important by both sheets. Reading 7 (Beyond Exceedance-Based Backtesting) is flagged as a new reading and 'highly testable'.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'backtesting VaR'; 'PIT vs exceedance': the point-in-time vs. exceedance-based distinction is the direct subject of Reading 7 and appears twice in the consolidated list. Kupiec's POF tests unconditional coverage only; Christoffersen adds independence, giving conditional coverage. Type I = rejecting a correct model; Type II = accepting a flawed one. Basel penalty zones (green/yellow/red) and their multiplier consequences are separately examinable. This pair remains uncleared in your Confusables Registry.

los.vardeez: Failure rates and model verification calculation (using the 2 tables)

selectors.name: Count exceptions against the model
selectors.what: Decide whether a VaR model is accurate from the number of exceptions (days the loss exceeds the previous day's VaR) in a sample: the failure-rate z test, z = (x - pT) / sqrt(p(1 - p)T), reject if |z| > 1.96, or Kupiec's LRuc against 3.841, or the non-rejection region read from the table for the VaR confidence level and sample length.
selectors.theory: Under the null the exception count is binomial with mean pT and variance p(1 - p)T; too many exceptions means risk is underestimated, too few means capital is used inefficiently; the test confidence level is not the VaR confidence level; passing on hypothetical but failing on actual returns points to intraday trading.

selectors.name: PIT-based versus exceedance-based backtesting
selectors.what: How the exceedance properties (unconditional coverage, independence) appear in a PIT backtest as PITs uniform on (0, 1) and independent; how a PIT is derived, p(t+1) = F(t)(P&L(t+1)); what the PIT histogram shape reveals (hump = conservative, spikes at 0 and 1 = aggressive); and the Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Anderson-Darling and Cramer-von Mises goodness-of-fit tests.

selectors.name: Kupiec versus Christoffersen
selectors.what: Kupiec's POF tests unconditional coverage (the exception count) only; Christoffersen's LRind tests independence of exceptions (one-lag clustering) and LRcc = LRuc + LRind is the conditional coverage test, chi-square with 2 degrees of freedom, critical value 5.991 (LRind and LRuc: 3.841).

selectors.name: Type I versus Type II errors
selectors.what: Type I is rejecting a correct model, Type II is failing to reject an incorrect one; the trade-off between them and how power (1 - Type II rate) rises with a longer sample or a lower VaR confidence level.

selectors.name: Basel penalty zones and multiplier
selectors.what: Basel traffic-light zones for exceptions of the 99% one-day VaR over 250 days: green 0 to 4 (plus factor 0), yellow 5 to 9 (plus 0.40, 0.50, 0.65, 0.75, 0.85), red 10 or more (plus 1.00); multiplier k = 3 + plus factor; and when a yellow-zone penalty applies and which exceptions may be excluded.
